proposals.title: One-article audio playback
proposals.trigger: While reading an article, the user taps a proposed Listen control.
proposals.userNeed: The user wants to finish the open article hands-free. A completed ad would unlock audio playback of that article once.
proposals.eligibility: Users reading an article whose publisher permits audio playback; exclude content the app cannot lawfully play.
proposals.productChange: Add a Listen control and one-article audio entitlement. Neither audio nor an audio gate was observed.
proposals.reward: One playback of the currently open article, not broader article access.
proposals.optIn: Show an optional sheet explaining the one-playback exchange; start the ad only after the user taps Watch ad.
proposals.fulfillment: After a completed ad, start playback on the open article and mark this playback as rewarded.
proposals.declinePath: Close the sheet and continue reading normally.
proposals.failurePath: If the ad is unavailable or unfinished, do not grant playback; return to the article with reading unaffected.
proposals.businessImpact: Could add ad revenue but may displace existing article ads or affect any paid audio benefit. Reading remains unchanged. Audio rights, delivery, and support may add costs.
proposals.validationPlan: Run an article-reader holdout experiment measuring completed playbacks, net ad revenue, existing-ad displacement, reading engagement, costs, and any paid conversion.
assumptions: Publisher audio rights and technical feasibility are unknown.
Ad fill, playback costs, paid benefits, and baseline business metrics are unknown.

proposals.title: One-article audio playback
proposals.trigger: While reading an open article, the user taps a proposed Listen control. Do not show the ad offer over a publisher access prompt.
proposals.userNeed: The reader wants to finish this article hands-free. One audio playback could help when reading is inconvenient.
proposals.eligibility: Only articles the user may already read and for which audio creation, playback, and ad-funded use are permitted. If a relevant paid audio offer exists, show that path first and consider the ad only after it is declined.
proposals.productChange: Add a Listen control, licensed audio delivery, and a one-playback reward. No audio feature, grant, or audio gate was observed. Preserve the publisher access prompt and existing article ads.
proposals.reward: One playback session for the open article only; no additional article access or repeat playback.
proposals.optIn: After Listen, show the one-playback exchange and start an ad only when the reader selects Watch ad.
proposals.fulfillment: On confirmed ad completion, start the article audio and mark that session as rewarded. Pausing and resuming within the session does not consume another reward.
proposals.declinePath: Dismiss the sheet and keep reading. Any publisher access or paid offer remains available.
proposals.failurePath: If no ad is available or it ends unfinished, grant no playback; return to the article without changing reading access.
proposals.businessImpact: Ad revenue might be offset by displaced article ads or paid conversion. Reading and publisher access remain unchanged. Rights, audio delivery, ad serving, and support could add costs.
proposals.validationPlan: First verify publisher rights and whether any paid audio benefit overlaps. If permitted, run an eligible-article reader holdout measuring completed sessions, incremental net ad revenue, article-ad displacement, reading engagement, costs, and paid conversion.
assumptions: Publisher audio and ad-funded playback rights are unknown.
Audio delivery quality, grant feasibility, ad fill, and costs are unknown.
Paid audio entitlements, prices, hands-free demand, and baseline business metrics are unknown.

proposals.title: Offline copy of a saved article
proposals.trigger: The user opens the observed Save this article action on a Home news item and chooses a proposed offline option.
proposals.userNeed: The user wants that news item available without a connection. A completed ad would prepare one offline copy while preserving ordinary saving.
proposals.eligibility: Users saving an article that the app is permitted and able to cache; ordinary Save remains available without an ad.
proposals.productChange: Add an optional offline-copy choice to the save action, plus caching and expiry handling. Offline saving and its grant were not observed.
proposals.reward: One eligible article cached for offline reading, subject to publisher permissions.
proposals.optIn: Present the offline option separately from ordinary Save; cache only after an affirmative Watch ad tap and completed ad.
proposals.fulfillment: Cache the selected article, confirm it is available offline, and leave the user on Home.
proposals.declinePath: Proceed with ordinary Save, or cancel the save action; neither requires an ad.
proposals.failurePath: If the ad is unavailable or unfinished, offer ordinary Save and do not claim an offline copy was created.
proposals.businessImpact: Could monetize offline demand, but may displace feed ads or affect an unknown paid offline benefit. Ordinary saving and browsing stay unchanged. Storage, downloads, and licensing may add costs.
proposals.validationPlan: Run a Home-save holdout experiment measuring incremental net ad revenue, ordinary saves, offline reads, feed-ad displacement, caching costs, and any paid conversion.
assumptions: The observed Save this article action does not establish offline capability or how saves work.
Caching rights, storage costs, paid benefits, ad fill, and baseline metrics are unknown.

proposals.title: Offline copy of a Home article
proposals.trigger: On Home, the user opens an article's observed “Save this article” action. A proposed, separate offline-copy option appears alongside ordinary Save. e9 only shows that the Save control appeared; it does not show a Save tap or its result.
proposals.userNeed: The user wants to read that article without a connection. After a completed ad, the app could cache one eligible article while leaving ordinary saving available.
proposals.eligibility: Offer only for an article with verified caching rights and technical support. Confirm that the offer does not bypass any paid offline entitlement before launch.
proposals.productChange: Add an optional offline-copy choice, local caching, an offline access point, and expiry handling. Neither offline access nor an ad-funded grant was observed.
proposals.reward: One eligible article cached for offline reading.
proposals.optIn: Keep ordinary Save available. Cache the selected article only after the user taps Watch ad and completes the ad.
proposals.fulfillment: Confirm the copy is ready, mark that article for offline access, and return the user to Home. The offline access point is proposed.
proposals.declinePath: Let the user use ordinary Save or cancel without watching an ad; do not change the existing Save behavior.
proposals.failurePath: If the ad is unavailable or unfinished, do not grant an offline copy. Leave ordinary Save available.
proposals.businessImpact: Offline reads might add ad revenue but displace feed ads or paid offline demand, if such a benefit exists. Browsing and ordinary saving remain unchanged. Downloads, storage, expiry handling, and licensing may add costs.
proposals.validationPlan: First verify the Save flow, caching rights, and paid benefits. Then run a Home-save holdout measuring completed offline reads and incremental net revenue after displaced ads and caching costs, alongside ordinary saves and paid conversion.
assumptions: e9 reveals a Save control after dismissing the location prompt, not how Save works.
Offline demand, caching rights, grantability, ad fill, costs, paid benefits, and baseline business metrics are unknown.
